label: end-of-input / <DEL> step in long sequences, boosted by first token (x,l,z,h,1,o) or last token (p,t,g,j,2,u,3)
explanation: Fires only around the end of the original input. About 79% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0) and the rest is on the last 1-3 original tokens (to_go 0-2), almost all at t=7-9. It never fires in the copy phase or at t<5. Rate and magnitude grow with length: nothing for L<=4, 11% of <DEL> steps at L>=7, 57% of mass at L=9. Content changes how often it fires: first_tok x (5.7x lift; x starts every top example), then l/z/h/1/o, and the token just before the current step (p,t,g,j,2,u,3). This looks like an additive length + first-token + last-token signal, so a boolean rule only gets about 0.55 F1. Plain phase==1 has 75% recall but 11% precision. Many long-sequence <DEL> steps that have the preferred tokens still do not fire, and low-level activations also show up with other tokens.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: x, z, l, h, 1, o; least: u, b, a, j) and the previous input (most: p, t, j, g, 2, u; least: f, n, l, x); timing cues that raise it most: t=8, t=7, L=9 & t=8.
